title: Manual match on Result/Option where let-else or combinators read better
description:
rust.md: "Prefer combinators (`.map()`, `?`, `and_then`) over nested `if let` chains when they're clearer" and "Prefer `?`, `map`, `and_then`, `map_err`, `ok_or` over manual `match` on `Result`/`Option`". `let ... else` is available at the declared MSRV (stable since 1.65).

Two-line `match` blocks whose only purpose is to bind-or-diverge:
- hire-attestors/src/ssh.rs:112-119 — two consecutive `match read_string(...) { Some(v) => v, None => break }` inside the key loop; `let Some((key_blob, rest)) = read_string(cur) else { break };` twice is shorter and puts the binding first
- hire-attestors/src/tailscale.rs:117-120 — `match fetch_status(...).await { Ok(s) => s, Err(_) => return Ok(FreshnessResult::Unavailable) }`
- hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs:97-100 — `match std::env::var("HOME") { Ok(h) => h, Err(_) => return vec![] }`; `let Ok(home) = ... else { return vec![] };`
- hire-nmh/src/main.rs:72-75 — `match read_message()? { Some(m) => m, None => break }`
- hire/src/main.rs:225-232, 309-316, 317-324, 366-373 — four `match opt { Some(a) => a, None => { eprintln!(...); exit(1) } }` blocks

Also in the same family, hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs:106-113: four levels of nested `if let` (`read_to_string` → `from_str` → `get("id_token")` → `claim_from_jwt`) that flatten to one `and_then` chain or a helper returning `Option`.

Nothing here is wrong, so this is polish — but the ssh.rs and oidc.rs nesting is where a future edit is most likely to attach a condition to the wrong level.
notes: PARTLY FIXED 2026-09-15. Fixed: hire-attestors/src/ssh.rs now uses let-else ('let Some((key_blob, rest)) = read_string(cur) else { break }'), and the tailscale.rs example is moot -- that freshness() override no longer exists. STILL OPEN: hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs's HOME match and its nested if-let chain; hire-nmh/src/main.rs's read_message match; and four exit-on-None matches in hire/src/main.rs.
